hint.label: Scale model
hint.text: A scale model is usually a smaller version of something big. It should have the exact same proportions as the original object.

atoms.text: Tony’s hobby is making scale models of different things. Can you help him with some of his latest projects?

instruction.text: Look at the dimensions of Tony’s model Viking ship compared to the real thing. How many times bigger is the real one?

hint.text: <mat>24 m=2400 cm</mat>. Use this information to work out the scale factor.
hint.sound: 24 metres is equal to 2,400 centimetres. Use this information to work out the scale factor.

instruction.text: Look at the dimensions of Tony’s model of the Elizabeth Tower compared to the real thing. How many times bigger is the real one?

hint.text: <mat>12 m=1200 cm</mat>. Use this information to work out the scale factor.
hint.sound: 12 metres is equal to 1,200 centimetres. Use this information to work out the scale factor.

instruction.text: Look at the dimensions of Tony’s model Brachiosaurus. What are the dimensions of a real one if it is 50 times bigger?
Look at the dimensions of the biplane. What are the dimensions of Tony’s model if it is 60 times smaller?
